statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail risk of 25% has crossed one point into the elevated band at its floor.
recommendation: Tail has reached the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The evidence-based danger window runs from the 13:30Z cash open through 15:30Z, covering the opening auction, the first full cash hour and the 14:00Z Factory Orders checkpoint. Tail is published at the floor of the elevated band because the pullback off the 31,222.25 session extreme has not yet failed. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ extends to a 31,222.25 52-week high after September payrolls undershoot at +29,000, and the U.S. cash open gaps the Nasdaq Composite 1.25% higher
body: NQ futures trade 31,171.00 (+410.50, +1.33%) on a quote timed 13:20:15Z, inside a session range of 30,760.25-31,222.25 against a 30,760.50 prior settlement, from a 30,771.25 open on about 145.9k contracts. The decisive observation is that 31,222.25 is both a new session high and the contract's 52-week high, and it is the third upside extension since the 12:30Z employment report: the high moved 31,035.25 to 31,105.50 to 31,222.25. Price now sits 51.25 points, or 0.16%, beneath that extreme, so the pullback off the high is shallow and still holding rather than failing. The 13:30Z U.S. cash open then gapped higher: the Nasdaq Composite printed 27,208.29 (+336.69, +1.25%) at 13:30:28Z against a 26,871.60 prior close, with only a 27,208.23-27,216.97 opening range so far, which is far too little data to call the auction. Cross-asset confirmation is broad. ES trades 7,792.25 (+0.88%) at 13:19:47Z, 10.50 points under its own 7,802.75 session high; Dow futures are 51,676.00 (+0.85%) and Russell 2000 futures 2,863.30 (+1.29%), so participation is wide rather than megacap-narrow. VIX is 15.60, down 0.79 or 4.82% from a 16.39 close, in a 15.49-16.24 range. The 2-year yields 4.752%, down 3.5bp with a 4.712% low, and the 10-year 5.205%, down 3.3bp in a 5.154%-5.262% range, with the 30-year near 5.57%. Notably the 10-year has already retraced 5.1bp up from its session low, so the bond leg of the alignment is loosening even as equities hold their highs. November WTI is $89.33, down 3.81%; gold $4,221.90 (+0.47%); bitcoin $86,650.37 (+3.28%). Semiconductors lead: SOXX traded $591.47 (+2.63%) premarket at 13:28:36Z, above its $579.98 prior-session high, and QQQ $751.57 (+1.29%) above its $744.67 prior-session high. The September employment report undershot materially. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported nonfarm payroll employment up 29,000 against a consensus near 84,000-90,000, with the unemployment rate at 4.2% from 4.1%. Average hourly earnings edged up 5 cents, or 0.1%, to $37.81, trimming annual growth to 3.0%. Prior months were revised 60,000 lower in combination: July by 31,000 from +21,000 to -10,000 and August by 29,000 from +162,000 to +133,000. Market-implied odds of an October rate hike fell from 64% to 16%. Company news is limited at the index level: Nike reported fiscal Q1 revenue of $11.21B against $11.33B expected and announced planned layoffs, with Lululemon, On and Deckers lower premarket. Tail is raised one point to 25%, the floor of the elevated band, on multiple independent current amplifiers rather than on the size of the release: repeated upside extension after the print, price holding within 0.16% of a fresh 52-week high, a shallow unfailed pullback, broad aligned cross-asset confirmation across VIX, the front and long end, oil, semiconductors and small caps, and a gap-up cash open layered on top of that alignment. That configuration is the one that historically denies mean reversion around a New York open. Three things argue against going further: the pullback has not yet failed, so repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement structure is unproven; the 10-year has already retraced off its low; and an absolute VIX of 15.60 with a 1.50% completed session range is not a violent repricing regime. Stress rises to 79% on that widened realized range and the carried 5.2% long-end regime. Confidence stays at 89%: current NQ, ES, Composite, VIX, both yields, oil, gold, semiconductor and QQQ levels plus the primary BLS release and a verified seven-day calendar are all in hand. The shared Finviz context was not used; its payload carries a 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z collection time and a partial collection status, so it is far outside the 90-minute freshness contract and contributes no evidence to this assessment.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band. Tail entered the window at 21% in the 13:00Z hour on 1 October, peaked at 24% at 14:00Z as long-end selling intensified, eased to 21% at 15:00Z, then printed 20% for fifteen consecutive hours across the U.S. afternoon and the Asian session before stepping to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. It returned to 20% at 10:00Z and 11:00Z once a genuine retracement formed, then printed 24% in the 12:00Z hour when the employment report took out the session high. Stress ranged from 74% to a 79% overnight peak and closed the window at 78%; Confidence held between 87% and 89%. Only the 08:00Z, 09:00Z and 12:00Z slots were published as trend-up; the other 21 hours were mixed.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 25% for the current 13:00Z hour containing the cash open and for the 14:00Z first full cash hour, which is the narrow window the amplifiers actually cover, then eases to 24% at 15:00Z and down to 21% by late afternoon as post-release repricing is assumed to complete. No slot is published above 25%, because going further would require observed repeated extension after failed retracements and the current pullback off 31,222.25 has not failed; that escalation condition is named explicitly on the two block hours instead, together with the retracement that would invalidate it. A one-point uplift to 22% covers the 19:00Z Friday power hour, where weekly-close flow meets a 52-week high, before Tail returns toward the watch floor at the 20:00Z cash close. CME equity index futures settle for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the final fifteen slots carry an explicit 20% watch floor for unknown state rather than a projection: a closed market offers no mean reversion to deny, and lowering those hours into the EA_ON band would misrepresent an unresolved 52-week-high close as benign. Confidence decays from 89% to 74% across that closed stretch while Tail and Stress hold, because evidence ageing degrades certainty about the state rather than the state itself. Next week's catalysts are Monday's 14:00Z ISM Services PMI and the Wednesday pairing of 12:30Z September CPI with the 18:00Z FOMC minutes, which is the next credible delayed-second-leg mechanism in the long end.
